name: Gallery and Cabinet Range
description: The Franco-Caribbean answer to a hot wet climate: four square rooms opening directly onto a full-width front gallery, with small cabinets flanking a rear loggia. There are no corridors, because the gallery is the corridor. It is the clearest demonstration in the catalogue that Anglo adjacency rules are regional rather than universal.

rooms.note: Front gallery and rear loggia; the front is public and the rear is family.
The cabinets: small rooms flanking the rear loggia, used for storage, stair or a spare bed.

internal_rules.statement: No interior corridor. Every room opens to the gallery and to its neighbour, and adding a hall destroys the ventilation the plan exists for.
Four openings across the front, no centred door. The symmetry is even-numbered, which reads wrong to an Anglo eye and is exactly correct.
The gallery is structural to the type, under the main roof or a continuous broken pitch, never applied to a finished wall.
Gallery depth not less than 8 ft, and the roof over it breaks pitch consistently all around where it breaks at all.
Openings align front to back so air crosses the full depth. A blocked enfilade of openings removes the reason the section is shaped this way.

attaches_to.position: the principal floor above the base

attaches_to.note: The passage is precisely what this type does without.

expansion_logic: The rear cabinet-loggia range fills in; the house grows backward and never forward past the gallery line.
servicing_strategy: Detached kitchen; the loggia carries the service route and the cabinets take the stair.

style_variation.note: The parent, with the same logic at larger scale.
The same range lifted a full storey on masonry, with an exterior ceremonial stair.

sources: Edwards, The Complex Origins of the American Domestic Piazza-Veranda-Gallery
Vlach, The Shotgun House: An African Architectural Legacy
